intervention.change: Keep the usual 4-sample plurality vote over the stored cued base samples, but break vote ties with an independent plain-prompt base sample instead of taking the lowest sample. A tie means no strict plurality among the finished samples' answers, grouped with rln4_lib.agree. The plain sample is the first T3.jsonl row per problem_index (base, plain, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384), with its answer extracted by grader v3 from its text. If the plain answer agrees with exactly one of the tied answer groups, pick that group. Otherwise, or if the plain row is a cap hit or has an empty extraction, fall back to the lowest-sample tie rule of result-5d032f. Problems that are not tied keep the usual vote. No new generation: the stored rows are reused.

cell.prompt: MATH-500 prompt with the three-token RL opening cue prefilled for the 4 voting samples; tie-breaker sample uses the plain prompt with no prefix (T3.jsonl)
cell.seeds: the stored seeds of studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0, samples 0-3, job 153825-208b) plus the stored seed of the first row per problem_index of r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl

intervention.count: Right answers over all 500 MATH-500 problems: a problem counts as right if the selected answer group contains a cued attempt-0 sample with score_v3 == 1. Cap-hit cued samples and samples with an empty extraction do not vote. A problem whose 4 cued samples all fail to finish counts as wrong. The plain sample only breaks ties and is never counted on its own.

best_known.setting: base + cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, vote over 4 after restart, ties to the shortest finished sample (19,697 tokens per problem)

intervention.why: The mechanism says each prompt fails on its own problem-specific traps, not on the cued base's set, so on the roughly 36 problems where the cued vote ties, an independent plain-prompt answer agrees with the right tied group more often than the lowest sample does (about 5 of 36 for the lowest sample). Plain errors still track difficulty, though, so this adds only about 3 to 5 problems over the 446 vote.
